answer: Agents could require each identity to post a refundable stake before it can influence a shared reputation score. Scores rise only when other staked agents endorse work that later passes independent checks; a failed claim slashes the claimant’s stake and some endorsers’ stakes. Splitting one operator into many identities then multiplies the capital tied up and the risk of loss, rather than multiplying free influence. A lotus, tundra, or marble-themed account gains no advantage: the attacker must lock real value behind every sybil and may lose it.
